text:
Mia Chen: Heads-up — marketplace joint announcement with AWS scheduled for next Tue. We need a clear driver/CUDA/ROCm pin + hotfix handoff so customers in the marketplace don't hit regressions.
Ajay Patel: +1. Are we asking partners to consume a single pinned tuple or allow fallback ranges?
Mia Chen: Prefer single pinned tuple for the announcement (simpler messaging). We should document recommended fallbacks for customers though.
Sophie Park: From product/comms perspective, we need to avoid promising a specific stack beyond the pinned tuple. Can we commit to a fallback policy for 30 days post-launch?
Lucas Rivera: Technical ask: we need exact PKG names and versions to bake into the marketplace VM/container. Suggest: nvidia-driver 535.86, cuda 12.2, libcudnn 9.1; ROCm: amdgpu-pro 6.6, rocm 5.6. I'll bench these on our internal perf harness.
Ashwin Iyer: Please note model perf was slightly worse on 5.6 vs 5.4 for long-contexts in last eval. We should include a performance note.
Ajay Patel: Partners: we should send a compatibility matrix doc and a tiny test harness. Will draft and loop partners.
Emily Zhao: Legal/marketplace checklist: make sure the listing copy says "compatible with pinned stack" and include a rollback contact. No mention of guaranteed performance numbers.
Mia Chen: Action list: 1) Lucas validate the tuple on AMI/container. 2) Ajay draft partner matrix + test harness. 3) Sophie prepare customer-facing language. 4) Emily add rollback/contacts. 5) Ops: create hotfix playbook.
Lucas Rivera: Working on step 1 — will run a 24h soak with traffic mix and KV-cache reuse scenario. Planning to run on r5g + g5 instances for marketplace images.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: marketplace-image-smoke -> staging (build-1842000001).
Ajay Patel: Draft matrix will include: pinned tuple, supported ranges, known regressions, mitigation steps, test commands. Example test snippet:
```
# quick GPU smoke for partners
python -m redwood_infer.smoke --model redwood-7b --batch 4 --seq 1024 --tokens 500
```
Mia Chen: Can we also add canary rollout plan for customers who use dedicated vs hosted? We should define traffic % and rollback thresholds.
Sophie Park: Proposed canary: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h with perf/cost/quality gates. If latency p95 increases >20% or rouge rate increases >2% revert.
Lucas Rivera: I'll add automated checks to the runtime: latency, OOMs, KV cache hit rate. If any of those fail the gating, pipeline halts.
Ashwin Iyer: For quality gates, tie to a small eval set (50 prompts) and compare embeddings + LM top-k divergence. I'll provide the eval pack.
Emily Zhao: For marketplace listing, include a contact alias: marketplace-hotfix@redwood.ai and a private SCIM channel with partners for urgent patches.
Ajay Patel: Partners already asked for hotfix cadence — propose 48h turnaround for security/critical regressions, 5 business days for non-critical.
Mia Chen: Sounds reasonable. Last: release freeze window? We should freeze major driver bumps 7 days before public announcement.
Lucas Rivera: Agreed — driver bumps outside maintenance window require partner sign-off.
Sophie Park: I'll draft the announcement language and the FAQ entries about pinned stacks and rollback.
Mia Chen: Cool. I'll send a one-pager to partners today with the pinned tuple, canary plan, and contact points.
Ajay Patel: I'll attach the initial compatibility matrix to that one-pager.
deploy-bot: staging build completed: marketplace-image-smoke (1842000123) -> all checks passed.
Lucas Rivera: Results from 24h soak: no OOMs, p95 latency +8%, KV hit stable. Will run the eval pack tomorrow and post results.
Ashwin Iyer: Eval pack ready; running now. Expect numbers within 12h.
Emily Zhao: I'll prep the marketplace legal copy and the rollback T&Cs.
Mia Chen: Thanks all — follow-ups as comments on the one-pager. If partners request broader ranges we will treat as a separate compatibility offering. :thumbsup:
